name: Slumbering Walker

abilities.text: At the beginning of your end step, you may remove a counter from ~. When you do, return target creature card with power 2 or less from your graveyard to the battlefield.

covers.line: ~ enters with two -1/-1 counters on it.

notes: Removing a counter is a negative counters effect on the source; the card only ever has -1/-1 counters, so that is the counter removed. 'When you do' is the reflexive trigger (CR 603.12), which fires only when the optional removal really happened.

issues: you may remove A COUNTER from this creature — expected a counter of ANY kind — if a +1/+1, stun or other counter has been put on it you may remove that one instead — scripted {op:'counters', target:'self', counter:'-1/-1', amount:-1} — hardcoded to -1/-1. The script's note ('the card only ever has -1/-1 counters') is false the moment any counter-placing effect touches it. — CR 122.1, 701.x

you may remove a counter from this creature. WHEN YOU DO, return target creature card ... — expected With no counters left, the removal is impossible, so it doesn't happen and the reflexive trigger never fires. — scripted addCounters (game.ts:307-313) with delta -1 on a permanent that has no -1/-1 counters deletes nothing but still emits a 'counter' event; emit bumps this.changes (game.ts:259), so lastHappened becomes true (game.ts:1058) and the reflexive at game.ts:1642 fires anyway — free graveyard recursion every end step once both counters are gone. — CR 603.12, 121.3

BLIND/SCENARIO NOTE — expected 'Declining to remove a counter returns nothing' should exercise the decline path — scripted The engine's may handling (game.ts:1649-1652) is correct; the scenario has no {"answer": false} step before {"resolve": true}, so the default agent accepts. That failure is a scenario-authoring gap, not evidence of a may/reflexive bug — but the decline path is untested. — CR 603.12
This creature enters with two -1/-1 counters on it. — expected as-enters counters — scripted asEnters [{kind:'counters', counter:'-1/-1', amount:2}] with a covers entry — correct. — CR 614.1c

you may remove A COUNTER from this creature — expected Remove a counter of any kind; if it has no counters, the removal cannot happen and the reflexive trigger does not fire. — scripted counters {target:'self', counter:'-1/-1', amount:-1}, hardcoded. addCounters (game.ts:307-313) with delta -1 on zero counters still emits a counter event, so this.changes moves and lastHappened becomes true (game.ts:1058) — the reflexive return fires even with no counters left, giving free graveyard recursion every end step. It also cannot remove a +1/+1 or stun counter another effect placed; the script's note ('the card only ever has -1/-1 counters') is false in general. — CR CR 121.3, 603.12

When you do, return target creature card with power 2 or less from your graveyard to the battlefield. — expected Reflexive trigger, fired only if the counter was actually removed; targets a creature card with power 2 or less. — scripted reflexive {when:'you-do'} + return-from-graveyard {powerLE:2, target:true} — the structure is right (game.ts:1642 gates on lastHappened); it is the lastHappened source above that is unsound. — CR CR 603.12

This creature enters with two -1/-1 counters on it. — expected Two -1/-1 counters as it enters (a replacement, not a trigger). — scripted asEnters counters '-1/-1' 2 with a covers entry. Correct. — CR CR 614.1c

Blind scenario 'Declining to remove a counter returns nothing' failed — expected Declining leaves the counters and returns nothing. — scripted Engine 'may' handling (game.ts:1649-1652) is correct; the scenario has no {"answer": false} step before {"resolve": true}, so the default agent accepted — a scenario-authoring gap, not proof of a may/reflexive bug, but it leaves the decline path untested.
